name: Example: Estimating the Value of a Function at a Point Given its Derivative
problem: Let $g$ be a function such that $g'(x) =\sqrt{x}$ and $g(4) = 3.$ Using the tangent line approximation of $g(x)$ at $x=4,$ estimate the value of $g(3.6).$
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $g(x)$ at the point $a=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =g(a)+{g}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =g(4)+{g}^{′}(4)(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $g(4)=3,$ and since $g'(x)=\sqrt{x},$ then $g'(4)=\sqrt{4}=2.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =3+2(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can approximate $g(3.6)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=3.6.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}g(3.6) & ≈L(3.6) \\  & =3+2(3.6-4) \\  & =3+2(-0.4) \\  & =3-0.8 \\  & =2.2.\end{aligned}
$$
